'''Sharrod Victor Ford''' (born January 9, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played briefly in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), as well as in a variety of top leagues around the world.

==Early years==
Ford attended [[Clemson University]] from 2001 to 2005. At Clemson, he became the school's first player to lead his team in points and rebounds for two consecutive seasons since [[Horace Grant]] in the 1980s.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/draft2005/profiles/SharrodFord.html Prospect Profile: Sharrod Ford ]</ref>

==Professional career==
Ford went undrafted at the [[2005 NBA draft]]. On November 2, 2005, he signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/175236/Suns-Sign-Ford-Waive-Tischer Suns Sign Ford, Waive Tischer]</ref> He was waived by the Suns on December 24, 2005, after appearing in three [[NBA]] league games.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/175881/Suns-Waive-Sharrod-Ford Suns Waive Sharrod Ford]</ref>

On January 10, 2006, he was acquired by the [[Fayetteville Patriots]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=3257236 Fayetteville Acquires Sharrod Ford]</ref> He appeared in 15 games for the Patriots.<ref name="dleague">[https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/f/fordsh01d.html Sharrod Ford D-League Stats]</ref> In February 2006, he moved to Germany and signed with [[Alba Berlin]] for the rest of the season. With Alba he won the 2006 [[German Basketball Cup|German Cup]].<ref name="euroleague">[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?clubcode=bam&pcode=LLX#!biography Euroleague.net profile]</ref> On July 31, 2006, he re-signed with Alba for one more season.<ref>[https://www.albaberlin.de/https://www.albaberlin.de/news/sharrod-ford-bleibt-bei-den-albatrossen-4265.html Sharrod Ford bleibt bei den Albatrossen] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054458/https://www.albaberlin.de/https://www.albaberlin.de/news/sharrod-ford-bleibt-bei-den-albatrossen-4265.html |date=March 4, 2016 }} {{in lang|de}}</ref>

For the 2007–08 season, he signed with the Italian club [[Sutor Basket Montegranaro|Sutor Montegranaro]]. For the 2008–09 season, he moved to [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]], also of Italy. With Bologna, he won the [[2008–09 FIBA EuroChallenge]].<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2009.roundID_6491.coid_4ihJxgKmGQ-HZmQI,0ZyJ2.articleMode_on.html Virtus BolognaFiere Beat Brave Cholet]</ref>

On September 18, 2009, he signed with [[BC Spartak Saint Petersburg|Spartak Saint Petersburg]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/eurocup/78893/spartak-inks-big-man-sharrod-ford.html Spartak inks big man Sharrod Ford]</ref> On November 16, 2009, he parted ways with Spartak.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/eurocup/79261/spartak-spb-waived-ford.html  Spartak SPB waived Ford]</ref> On January 10, 2010, he returned to Italy, and signed with [[Basket Club Ferrara]], for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/79578/ferrara-goes-big-with-sharrod-ford.html Ferrara goes big with Sharrod Ford]</ref> On July 19, 2010, he returned to his former team. Sutor Montegranaro. for the 2010–11 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/83337/sutor-montegranaro-sharrod-ford-is-back.html Sutor Montegranaro, Sharrod Ford is back]</ref>

On July 21, 2011, he signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/87537/bayern-munich-announces-robin-benzing-je-kel-foster-and-sharrod-ford.html Bayern Munich announces Robin Benzing, Je'Kel Foster and Sharrod Ford]</ref> However, he left the team during the pre-season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/88482/sharrod-ford-leaves-bayern-munich.html Sharrod Ford leaves Bayern Munich]</ref> In February 2012, he joined the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the NBA D-League, but left after only 6 games.<ref name="dleague"/>

On August 20, 2012, he signed with the German club [[Brose Baskets]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99270/180/brose-baskets-lands-sharrod-ford Brose Baskets lands Sharrod Ford]</ref> With Brose Baskets, he won the [[2012–13 Basketball Bundesliga|2012–13 Bundesliga]], and the 2013 [[BBL Champions Cup]].<ref name="euroleague"/> On July 29, 2013, he re-signed with Brose for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/104328/brose-baskets-bamberg-keep-sharrod-ford.html Brose Baskets Bamberg keep Sharrod Ford]</ref>

On June 30, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[Paris-Levallois Basket|Paris-Levallois]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20151208095322/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138286/paris-levallois-tabs-veteran-big-man-ford Paris-Levallois tabs veteran big man Ford]</ref> On April 16, 2015, he was named to the [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup Second Team]], after averaging 15.1 points and 8.8 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150417193341/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/5w4x8nukoug5cxca/2014-15-all-eurocup-first-second-teams-announced 2014-15 All-Eurocup first, second teams announced]</ref>

On July 24, 2015, he signed with [[Acıbadem Üniversitesi S.K.|Acıbadem Üniversitesi]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Second League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/170313/sharrod-ford-signs-in-tb2l-with-acibadem-istanbul.html Sharrod Ford signs in TB2L with Acibadem Istanbul]</ref> On August 3, 2016, he re-signed with Acıbadem Üniversitesi for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/208585/sharrod-ford-re-signs-with-acibadem-universitesi.html Sharrod Ford re-signs with Acibadem Universitesi]</ref>
